key_insight: The paper reframes sparse triangular solve graph transformation as a reinforcement learning problem, enabling matrix-specific rewiring that balances parallelism gains with workload regularity.
engineering_relevance: This can improve SpTRSV performance in scientific computing pipelines by reducing dependency depth and balancing level costs, which is important for efficient parallel execution on real sparse matrices.
method: Formulate graph transformation as a sequential decision-making task over the matrix dependency graph.
Train an RL agent to learn transformation policies tailored to each matrix’s sparsity structure.
Use curriculum learning and fine-tuning to transfer learned policies to unseen matrices.
evidence_signal: Across real-world sparse matrices, the method achieved up to 94% level reduction and up to 80% lower coefficient of variation in level costs, with an average 23% fewer levels and 29% lower variability while rewriting only 0.82% of rows on average.
watch_item: The learned policies may not generalize well across very different sparsity patterns, and the implementation must manage the tradeoff between aggressive level reduction and improved load balance.
paper_title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Graph Transformations for SpTRSV Optimization
